## Scope of review

All 24 upstream SKILL.md files were enumerated. The README and MIT license were inspected. The 11 selected skill documents were fetched individually and reviewed in full. The selected subset is plain Markdown guidance, without bundled executable scripts or package dependencies. Source instructions include shell examples in some non-selected/deferred documents; no scripts or package manifests are imported. Cross-skill references are not treated as installed dependencies.

- client-vetting

## Deferred / excluded in this pass

- `client-onboarding`, `context-switch`, `dev-handoff`, `project-closeout`: require system/account access, access transfer/removal, or environment verification.
- `deploy-verify`, `incident-response-solo`: include production/deploy/rollback workflows; review-only adaptation needed before any future intake.
- `security-baseline-audit`: security-sensitive remediation and secret rotation; report-only safe adaptation required.
- `subcontractor-brief`: third-party access and client delivery control require additional permission design.
- `bug-triage`, `change-request`, `estimate-postmortem`, `expense-and-time-tagging`, `late-payment-followup`: useful candidates, but need further detailed adaptation/testing and/or invoice, payment, or client-communication safeguards.

## Mandatory restrictions

- Skills are documentation, not executable code. CEOAI code-owned policy and allowlists remain authoritative.
- No autonomous client contact, email sending, job applications, account creation, access granting, contract acceptance/signature, deployment, production mutation, invoice sending, payment collection, or transfers.
- Contract outputs are not legal advice; refer jurisdiction-specific decisions to qualified counsel.
- Do not infer or fabricate client facts, work hours, rates, scope, evidence, payment terms, or legal rights.
- Any financial calculation is an estimate from supplied evidence; never initiate a financial action.
- No secrets in chat or documents. Credentials must never be requested or accepted through chat.
- User approval is required before every external side effect; app-level security gates still apply.
